body: Sunday, August 09 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Fed under new Chair Warsh has signaled a smaller footprint in markets, holding rates steady amid conflicting data. Fiscal spending remains expansionary. The 10Y yield has risen to 4.66% (+9 bps vs 4W ago) while the 2Y sits at 4.19% (prior close, −2 bps vs 4W), producing a +46 bps curve — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards — with the steepening reflecting term premium re-pricing rather than imminent easing. VIX at 14.90 screams complacency.

New / Most Important: July payrolls shocked with a loss of 23,000 jobs — the first negative print in years — yet equities rallied (S&P 500 at 7757, ↑2.4% vs 4W). This is a structurally important divergence. The market is treating bad labor data as good news for eventual rate cuts, but Warsh's philosophical shift toward less market hand-holding means the "Fed put" strike price is much lower than the market assumes. The US also actively sold euros and intervened jointly with Japan to prop up the yen — an extraordinary and historically rare move for the Treasury to intervene against its own currency's trading partners. Bessent's comments nudging BOJ toward a September hike confirm this is a coordinated Plaza Accord-lite framework. CPI data due this week will be the critical test of whether Warsh can maintain the hold posture.

Playbook ✓: Equity markets making new highs on breadth expansion (Russell ↑1.9%, R/N ratio ↑2.3%) fits the late-cycle rotation playbook; gold surging (4399, ↑7.2%) on fiscal concerns and real-rate anxiety is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The combination of negative payrolls, rising long-end yields, AND equities at all-time highs is genuinely anomalous. This is not a "bad news is good news" rate-cut trade — long yields are rising, not falling. What's happening is a liquidity-driven melt-up where capital flows into US equities as a default allocation even as the macro deteriorates. Gold at 4399 (↑7.2%) alongside S&P records suggests the equity rally is narrow in its macro conviction — big money is hedging with gold even as it buys stocks. If CPI comes in hot this week, the contradiction resolves violently to the downside. If CPI is cool, Warsh faces enormous pressure to cut into negative payrolls, but his stated philosophy resists that. Either outcome is explosive.

Macro Stance: ECB in a gradual easing cycle, but hawkish bets have resurfaced as EUR/USD finds fresh upside support. The DXY holding near 99–100 (feed shows pressure near 99.65) reflects genuine dollar weakness benefiting the euro.

New / Most Important: The US Treasury sold euros as part of the coordinated yen intervention — blindsiding the ECB according to FT reporting. This is a major development: the US effectively used EUR as funding currency for FX intervention without prior ECB coordination, undermining Lagarde's policy autonomy. The ECB's new BIG index for tracking credit conditions suggests internal concern about transmission mechanism effectiveness. Hawkish ECB bets supporting EUR upside imply markets see the ECB pausing or slowing cuts relative to prior expectations.

Playbook ✓: EUR strengthening on relative rate differentials narrowing is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The US unilaterally selling euros to buy yen is a structural break in the post-GFC central bank coordination framework. If this becomes a pattern — the US using EUR as a funding tool for geopolitical currency management — it transforms the ECB's rate path into a second-order variable driven by US Treasury preferences rather than eurozone fundamentals. The ECB being "blindsided" suggests this was not a consensual G7 operation but a bilateral US-Japan move with collateral damage to Europe. European policymakers may need to respond with their own intervention toolkit or accept euro appreciation that tightens financial conditions beyond what the ECB intends. This is a new regime for EUR crosses.

Macro Stance: July prices removed an obstacle to easing. CPI edged up 0.5% and PPI growth slowed to 3.5%, both missing expectations (BigGo Finance, [Aug 8]); consumer inflation is at a six-month low (TradingView, [Aug 8]) and factory-gate inflation at a 3-month low (Reuters, [Aug 8]), cooling as the impact of the Iran war eases (Financial Times, [Aug 8]), after June's 1.0% CPI and 4.1% PPI (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 8]). The PBOC had already pledged timely adjustment of its policy tools (Reuters, [Aug 2]), and China Daily writes that interest rate and RRR cuts may be on the table ([Aug 4]). Reserve management is active: the central bank extended its gold buying to 21 months with the largest purchase since 2023 (Caixin Global, [Aug 8]), while July FX reserves rose less than expected (The Standard, [Aug 7]). The yuan is firm near a 3-1/2-year high on robust exports (The Star, [Aug 7]).

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and the non-manufacturing PMI to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]); the private factory index eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]), a 4-month low (Reuters, [Aug 2]). Trade carries the economy, though the headlines need reconciling. Exports surged 23.9% and the surplus widened to $112.5B (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 7]), yet SCMP says the surplus narrowed ([Aug 7]) and AP that exports slowed slightly ([Aug 7]): growth eased from June's 27% (Reuters, [Jul 13]) and the surplus shrank from June while still beating forecasts (TradingView, [Aug 6]); the widening is against a year earlier. Total trade expanded 19.2% in July (CGTN, [Aug 7]) as AI demand lifted export prices (Caixin Global, [Aug 7]). Domestic demand is the gap after Q2 GDP growth of 4.3% fell below the target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]).

Credit Impulse: The July credit data are still to come and the previews conflict. A Reuters poll sees bank lending set to plummet on subdued demand and a seasonal slowdown ([Aug 7]), while Caixin expects loans to rebound on a low base ([Aug 7]). Reconciled: a sharp drop from June's seasonal peak that still compares well with a weak July last year. VT Markets reads July credit demand as weak, with low loan growth fuelling easing bets ([Aug 8]). June set the tone: new loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]) and household loans fell 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]). Record low yields on long-dated offshore yuan bonds (Bloomberg, [Aug 4]) are the market's verdict on demand.

Property: Policy is moving in the top tier: Beijing further relaxed home-buying curbs (Reuters, [Aug 7]), following Shanghai (Bloomberg, [Aug 7]). The data explain the urgency. Housing prices fell 0.5% in July as sales volume weakened (Investing.com, [Aug 3]), the top-100 developer sales slump deepened (Trivium China, [Aug 5]) and property investment slumped 18 percent y/y in January–June (The Standard, [Jul 15]), even as June new home prices fell at a slower pace (Reuters, [Jul 14]). China Cinda warns of a first-half profit drop as the slump weighs (Caixin Global, [Aug 5]), and PIIE argues the property bust is spilling across China's borders ([Aug 7]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: SCMP reads the Politburo as cautious confidence ([Aug 3]), and Oxford Economics says an unspent fiscal arsenal targets a Q3 recovery (CNBC, [Aug 3]). The surprise tax on offshore trusts (CNBC, [Aug 4]) reaches offshore insurance income (Reuters, [Aug 6]), and a crackdown on capital outflow has hit Macau casinos (The Edge Singapore, [Aug 7]). Trade risk escalated: the US Senate cleared a Russia sanctions bill carrying 100% tariffs on India and China (Business Standard, [Aug 8]), though some senators oppose it (News18, [Aug 8]). That comes on top of a 15% US tariff on polysilicon (Nikkei Asia, [Aug 7]), while China's rare-earth exports to Japan and the US plunged after restrictions (Nikkei Asia, [Aug 8]).

Markets & Flows: China and Hong Kong stocks rose as strong trade data and AI demand lifted sentiment (The Economic Times, [Aug 7]), and cheap Chinese AI is shifting investors' focus to internet stocks (Moneyweb, [Aug 8]). Earlier in the week the Hang Seng slumped nearly 500 points as insurers sank (The Standard, [Aug 6]). Flows stay supportive: mainland investors extended their Hong Kong buying spree (South China Morning Post, [Aug 5]), Morgan Stanley lifted its Hang Seng target to 28,400 (BigGo Finance, [Aug 5]) and Chinese investors poured $1.2bn into gold ETFs (TradingView, [Aug 6]). NerdWallet's list of best-performing China stocks for August shows retail attention returning.

New / Most Important: July inflation cooled more than expected, with CPI at a six-month low and PPI at a 3-month low, just as previews point to weak July loan demand. With the PMIs below 50 and the yuan near a 3-1/2-year high, the case for the rate and RRR cuts China Daily has floated is now stronger. The Senate's 100% tariff bill is the risk that could force the timing.

Playbook ✓: Cooling inflation, easing signals, top-tier property relaxation and AI-led exports are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Consensus treats cooling PPI as relief; with the PMIs contracting and loan demand weak, it reads more like fading demand. Iron ore at a year low (Tech Times, [Aug 4]) leaves AUD exposed into this week's RBA decision. European exporters face a Germany-China trade imbalance that widened further in July (Ghana Business News, [Aug 8]), and the Senate bill hits India and China together, a double shock for EM Asia. With oil at $78.18, cooling factory-gate prices squeeze margins further.
Macro Stance: BOJ on a clear tightening path with September hike expectations firmly embedded. Fiscal stance neutral. The yen intervention has been the dominant macro story globally.

New / Most Important: This week's developments around the coordinated US-Japan yen intervention represent the most significant FX policy event since the Plaza Accord. The US actively supported yen strength — Reuters and CNBC detailed how Bessent and Japanese officials structured the bilateral pact to squeeze yen shorts. Bessent publicly stated confidence that BOJ's Ueda will "do what is best," which is diplomatic code for "hike in September or we'll have a problem." PM Takaichi is being pressured to align with BOJ's tightening — a notable political shift since she was previously seen as a dove. BOJ has lined up additional speaking events ahead of the September meeting, telegraphing intent. This is structurally new: the US has never in the modern era actively intervened to weaken its own currency against the yen while simultaneously pressuring the partner central bank to tighten. The implication is that the US views yen weakness as a financial stability threat (carry trade unwinds, Treasury market dysfunction) serious enough to warrant sacrificing dollar strength. For capital flows, this redirects Japanese institutional money back home — the largest pool of overseas fixed-income capital in the world begins to repatriate.

Playbook ✓: Yen strengthening and BOJ hawkishness are consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The US actively helping is NOT consensus — most desks had modeled unilateral Japan intervention with US tacit approval at best. Active US euro selling to fund yen support is a completely different animal with implications across every G10 cross.

Macro Stance: RBA decision imminent this week with markets pricing a potential cut, but the signal feed is deeply conflicted — AFR argues the RBA should actually raise rates, while domestic inflation remains "a key risk." Forward guidance has effectively died ("death of forward guidance" per AFR).

New / Most Important: The ASX hit a record high ahead of the RBA decision, buoyed by miners rallying on Strait of Hormuz diplomacy optimism. The debate is genuinely two-sided: some strategists argue for a hike given sticky domestic inflation, while SBS and others flag rate relief expectations. The RBA going silent on forward guidance is itself a structural shift — it removes the market's ability to position ahead of meetings, increasing vol around each decision. MFS IM called a rate hike a "reasonably small chance," which is notable because any non-zero probability of a hike when the market expects a cut creates asymmetric risk.

Playbook ✓: Commodity-linked equity rally on oil strength and on copper as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, even with iron ore at a year low.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The fact that serious voices are calling for a hike while others expect a cut means the RBA decision this week is a genuine coin-flip with massive AUD and rates vol implications. Position accordingly with straddles, not directional bets.

Macro Stance: NBP has been holding rates as inflation remains above target, and the week ahead decides the tone: Gazeta Prawna [Aug 9] previews the inflation and balance-of-payments data due after the weekend, and ING [Aug 7] lists Polish GDP and inflation on the CEE calendar. Parkiet [Aug 9] notes the easy money on deposits is over and real returns now depend on inflation. The internal debate is unresolved: Glapiński is reported to want lower rates against expert objections (Super Biznes, [Aug 3]), analysts weigh a September cut (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 6]), and the bank is also in an argument with the ECB, which is assessing the NBP's controversial plan to sell gold (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 6]) and the transfer of profit to defence (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 7]). Growth gives no cover for easing: analysts raised their GDP forecasts (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 3]), Interia Biznes [Aug 5] sees up to 4.1% possible, the PMI rebounded with the first rise in employment in months (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 3]) and Euronews [Aug 9] confirms Poland is now the EU's sixth-largest economy, ahead of Belgium and Austria. The one soft spot is agriculture, with drought cutting the grain harvest by close to 5% (PKB24.pl, [Aug 3]).

Markets: Friday's closes leave the index just above its breakout: WIG20 fell while mWIG40 set a record (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 7]) but held 4000 points (Bankier, [Aug 7]), after a mid-week dip of 0.29% on Wednesday (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 5]). The card shows the rotation of the past month: KGHM 352.95 (+14.6% 1W, +14.2% 4W) and PGE 10.75 (+6.3% 1W, +14.7% 4W) carry the week, consumer names carry the month with Allegro 46.21 (+16.0% 4W), Dino 32.44 (+15.0% 4W), LPP 22,220 (+14.7% 4W) and CD Projekt 256.1 (+9.9% 4W), while the financials that led the breakout have stalled, PKO 109.0 (-2.6% 1W, -3.4% 4W) and Pekao 252.9 (+3.0% 1W, +3.5% 4W), and Orlen 149.06 (+0.7% 1W, +6.5% 4W) gave back its results pop (Comparic, [Aug 7]). EPOL 44.19 is +3.2% 1W and +9.5% 4W. The zloty: USD/PLN 3.7297 (-0.2% 1W, -1.5% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.2961 (-0.2% 1W, -0.7% 4W); the euro has been fighting to break 4.30 (Bankier, [Aug 5]) and weak US labour data have weighed on the dollar (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 7]), so PLN benefits from broad EUR strength and EM carry appetite. POLGBs rebounded at the start of August (Bankier, [Aug 7]) and households bought nearly 10 bn zł of retail Treasury bonds in July (Bankier, [Aug 7]).

Fiscal & Politics: Rzeczpospolita [Aug 9] asks whether Poland has just crossed the constitutional debt limit, days after Konkret24 [Aug 7] answered the same question with "it depends"; public spending is 50.9% of GDP, above Germany, Sweden and Denmark (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 5]), the state costs over 53 thousand zł per Pole (Interia Biznes, [Aug 5]) and wGospodarce [Aug 8] says the budget's fate hangs on the EU SAFE loan. Against that, the election sausage is roasting: Gazeta Prawna [Aug 9] prices the higher tax-free allowance and second tax threshold at up to 70 bn zł, Bloomberg [Aug 4] reported income tax relief for millions being weighed, and Domański says the budget bill will come this month with the allowance work ongoing (Pit.pl, [Aug 7]) while the MF assembles a 2027 budget with the EU's largest deficit (pb.pl, [Aug 4]). Poland has also published draft legislation introducing a digital services tax (EY, [Aug 6]).

Corporate & Sectors: Housing is the weekend's fresh signal: home sales are accelerating and developers' supply has started to shrink (Bankier, [Aug 9]). Retail: LPP, with sales up 18.5%, plans as many as 750 new Sinsay stores this year (Wiadomości Handlowe, [Aug 9]); DlaHandlu.pl [Aug 9] reports Dino, Biedronka and Lidl will have to disclose private-label producers. Banks: the CHF law is in force and borrowers may stop paying instalments once they sue (Do Rzeczy, [Aug 9]), borrowers are warned not to sign WIBOR-to-POLSTR annexes blind (Bizblog.pl, [Aug 9]), lenders may be heading for a wave of credit refusals (Zero.pl, [Aug 8]). Energy: compensation for curtailing renewables has exceeded 100 mn zł (Interia Biznes, [Aug 9]), heat and power-market dynamics are feeding food prices (Energetyka24, [Aug 9]), the nuclear contractor has taken over the site (Radio Bezpieczna Podróż, [Aug 9]) though Fakt [Aug 8] reports hard American negotiating and possible delay. Orlen moved on fuel prices for the first time in months (DlaHandlu.pl, [Aug 8]) after a 7.7 bn zł quarter (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 7]) and an indictment over 1.5 bn zł of damage (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 7]).

Geopolitics & Security: General Kraszewski says the Lublin-region explosion taught the Russians the state of Poland's civil defence systems (Polskie Radio Lublin, [Aug 9]), as the US intelligence assessment that Putin may test NATO with a limited attack on Poland or the Baltics keeps circulating (The Week, [Aug 8]); the foreign minister wants allies to reconsider intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine (The New Voice of Ukraine, [Aug 6]) and talks on a permanent US base continue (NDTV, [Aug 5]).

New / Most Important: The constitutional debt question. When the national paper of record asks whether the constitutional ceiling has been breached in the same week the government prices 70 bn zł of pre-election tax cuts and admits the budget rests on an EU defence loan, the fiscal premium stops being an abstraction. It arrives before a GDP and CPI week and with the NBP fighting the ECB over gold and profit transfers; POLGBs have rebounded, which is exactly where a reassessment would show first.

Playbook ✓: Rates held and PLN steady; the data week is the next catalyst.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today — PLN benefits from broad EUR strength and EM carry appetite, but no catalyst for repositioning until the debt-limit question is answered by the budget bill rather than by commentators.
Macro Stance: Dollar weakness (DXY near 99–100) is broadly supportive for EM. Indonesia's growth remains modest per Standard Chartered amid global headwinds.

New / Most Important: Nigeria's President Tinubu publicly celebrated stock market rebound and economic team performance — a political narrative that often precedes policy complacency. Korean stock market volatility may be easing per Bloomberg as leveraged positions unwind and regulation takes hold. Indonesia flagged as modest growth — a relative underperformer in ASEAN.  |  Playbook ✓: EM benefiting from dollar weakness.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Korea's de-leveraging is constructive for medium-term positioning; the forced unwind of leveraged retail positions creates a cleaner base for institutional entry.
Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 at 29722 is down 0.3% vs 4W while the S&P is up 2.4%: tech lags a broadening market, and software has split on who can show AI revenue. Cisco earnings are ahead this week.

Reported: Palantir soared 12% on a blowout quarter as U.S. commercial revenue rose nearly 150% (CNBC, [Aug 3]) and raised guidance again (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 4]). Atlassian beat and the stock jumped 37.4% (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). Datadog had its worst day in more than 6 years despite a beat (Barron's, [Aug 6]), as its results and HubSpot's raised questions over AI pricing (Investor's Business Daily, [Aug 6]).

EPS Upside Watch: Arista Networks — UBS raised its price target on strong results (Investing.com Canada, [Aug 5]) after a $2.1 billion projection boost (RealMoney Pro, [Aug 5]). Microsoft — Citi raised its target to $600 after the Azure earnings beat (Mitrade, [Aug 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Russell/Nasdaq ratio is up 2.3% over 4 weeks as capital rotates out of mega-cap tech into small caps, and the 'SaaSpocalypse' debate has software stocks swinging wildly (CNBC, [Aug 7]). AI pricing doubts, not rates, are now the sector's real discount factor.
Narrative: Ad-spend resilience and the broad equity rally carry the sector, with Meta and Alphabet still the drivers; the open question is how evenly the ad budget is spread.

Reported: Snap's stock jumped 8% on an earnings beat and a strong sales forecast (CNBC, [Aug 3]), helped by a World Cup ad boost (BigGo Finance, [Aug 3]). Disney topped earnings estimates as parks and streaming offered a boost (CNBC, [Aug 5]). Pinterest slid 9% as a weak Q3 outlook overshadowed its earnings beat (TIKR.com, [Aug 5]).

EPS Upside Watch: Deutsche Telekom — lifted its buyback by up to $3.5 billion and raised guidance for a key metric again (WSJ, [Aug 6]), a per-share lever on top of operating growth. Versant Media — raised its 2026 outlook on its platforms segment and advertising momentum (CNBC, [Aug 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Ad-spend resilience is not lifting all of ad tech: The Trade Desk plunged 28% after an earnings miss while AppLovin and Magnite held firm (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 7]), and Criteo cut full-year guidance again as ad-tech earnings split in two (PPC Land, [Aug 5]). Share of the budget, not the size of the budget, is the call.
Narrative: The +46 bps 10Y-2Y curve (11 bps steeper vs 4W) and a 10Y at 4.66% are a modest NIM tailwind on new lending, and the quarter showed wealth and fee income doing the heavy lifting.

Reported: HSBC's profit jumped 23% as Asia wealth fuelled earnings (Nikkei Asia, [Aug 4]), and its earnings beat came with resumed stock buybacks (Quartz, [Aug 4]). DBS shares scaled a record high as the bank lifted its forecast after a profit beat (Reuters, [Aug 6]). Fiserv cut its 2026 outlook as Q2 earnings and revenue missed estimates (Proactive financial news, [Aug 6]).

EPS Upside Watch: Corpay — beat on corporate payments strength and brokers raised their price targets (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). Upstart — loan originations jumped 50% as it preps a bank launch (PYMNTS.com, [Aug 5]), volume that feeds straight into earnings.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Negative July payrolls should be a credit-quality warning, yet banks are rallying on the steeper curve: the market prices NIM expansion over credit deterioration, a bet that works until unemployment crosses the threshold that triggers loss provisions. Credit-card ABS spreads are the place to watch this week.

Narrative: WTI at 78.18 (↑9.5% vs 4W) is a supply-shock move, not demand-pull, with China's official manufacturing PMI in contraction at 49.2; Strait of Hormuz diplomacy eases the supply premium but keeps a geopolitical bid alive.

Reported: BP's quarterly profit doubled to over $5 billion after the Iran war oil surge (Reuters, [Aug 4]). Saudi Aramco's profits jumped 33% in the second quarter as the war squeezed oil supply (CNBC, [Aug 4]). ExxonMobil's stock dropped after a Q2 earnings miss against Wall Street targets (TIKR.com, [Aug 2]).

EPS Upside Watch: Chevron — analysts raised their forecasts after upbeat Q2 earnings (Benzinga, [Aug 3]). Inpex — raised its full-year guidance on higher oil prices and an LNG project (Reuters, [Aug 7]), price and volume working together.

⚡ Breaking Convention: US drillers adding Permian rigs into a supply-shock rally will eventually cap prices, but the political cap is arriving first: Trump blasted Exxon and Chevron for making 'too much money' and demanded lower gasoline prices (Reuters, [Aug 4]), and calls for a windfall tax on Big Oil's Iran-war profits are growing (The Guardian, [Aug 7]).

Narrative: Small-cap outperformance (Russell ↑1.9%) favours domestic industrials and infrastructure spending stays supportive, but the earnings leadership this season is AI power and data-centre capex.

Reported: Caterpillar beat forecasts and its shares jumped 9% (Investing.com, [Aug 4]) as it lifted its 2026 sales growth target on strong data-centre demand (CNBC, [Aug 4]). Siemens rode the AI boom to its highest-ever industrial profit (Reuters, [Aug 6]). Honeywell Aerospace plunged 24% after a guidance cut (AskTraders, [Aug 6]), as supply constraints dampened second-quarter sales (WSJ, [Aug 5]).

EPS Upside Watch: Eaton — analysts boosted their forecasts after a strong Q2 (Benzinga, [Aug 3]), sitting where data-centre power meets grid hardening. Rockwell — reported organic growth and raised its guidance (the Electrical Distributor magazine, [Aug 4]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bull case runs through AI power more than domestic small caps: Caterpillar's sales passed $20B as data-centre generators took off (Manufacturing Dive, [Aug 5]). Honeywell Aerospace shows the binding limit is supply, not demand — capacity-constrained names can cut guidance even in a boom.
Narrative: The K-shaped economy is the lens: the loss of 23,000 jobs in July and higher energy costs squeeze the lower-income consumer, while affluent households keep spending.

Reported: McDonald's US sales missed estimates as the CEO tapped a new US leader — 'We simply didn't execute' (New York Post, [Aug 4]). Wayfair jumped 30% as it posted its strongest US growth since 2020 (CNBC, [Aug 4]). Uber sank 5% after weak guidance despite revenue growth (CNBC, [Aug 5]).

EPS Upside Watch: Next — raised its profit outlook again as warm weather boosted summer sales (Reuters, [Aug 5]). Etsy — analysts increased their forecasts after a better-than-expected Q2 (Benzinga, [Aug 7]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The K-shape cuts both ways: high-income shoppers drove Wayfair's revenue gains (Retail Dive, [Aug 4]) while the poor are spending less at McDonald's (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 5]). The short belongs on mass-market names; the affluent-exposed end of XLY is still beating.

Narrative: Defensive positioning benefits from the negative payrolls print and the K-shaped economy, and staples outperform discretionary in a stagflationary pocket, though input costs are testing margins.

Reported: Kraft Heinz beat and raised its annual forecast (Quartz, [Aug 5]). Tyson Foods cut its profit forecast as tight US cattle supplies hurt its beef business (Reuters, [Aug 3]). Nivea maker Beiersdorf cut its 2026 guidance, citing a difficult market (Reuters, [Aug 3]).
EPS Upside Watch: ADM — lifted its 2026 profit forecast on strong margins and a favorable biofuels outlook (Reuters, [Aug 4]). Henkel — raised its organic growth guidance for 2026 (Reuters, [Aug 5]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Trade-down is not lifting brands: Celsius plunged 17% toward a 16-month low after missing estimates (BigGo Finance, [Aug 6]), while Ahold Delhaize beat its profit view on cost cuts (Reuters, [Aug 5]). Staples upside is coming from cost and pricing levers, not volume.
Narrative: Healthcare is a defensive holding helped by rotation out of growth into value, but returns are being set by single-stock guidance — obesity drugs above all.

Reported: Eli Lilly easily topped estimates and raised its outlook as Zepbound and Mounjaro sales surged (CNBC, [Aug 5]). Novo Nordisk's outlook hike fell flat as Wegovy pill sales failed to impress (Reuters, [Aug 4]). Pfizer beat earnings estimates and targeted $2.5 billion in additional cost cuts (Reuters, [Aug 4]).

EPS Upside Watch: McKesson — lifted its full-year EPS target as North American pharma profit soared 19% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 5]). Halozyme — posted a record quarter, beat estimates and raised its full-year 2026 guidance (PR Newswire, [Aug 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Obesity is turning winner-take-most: Lilly widened its gap with Novo on resilient demand for injectable GLP-1 drugs (Reuters, [Aug 5]), while Lilly's own obesity pill disappointed in Q2 (Fierce Pharma, [Aug 5]). The pill trade both companies were priced for has not arrived; injectables still carry the earnings.

Narrative: Copper ↑5.7%, bid as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, and gold ↑7.2% to 4399 drive the sector; gold miners are the standout, while China's contracting July PMIs keep bulk producers out of favour.

Reported: Glencore's half-year earnings rose 86% to $10bn (Mining Weekly, [Aug 5]) on a trading windfall (Reuters, [Aug 5]). MP Materials beat expectations on rising sales and US price support (Reuters, [Aug 6]). Smurfit Westrock cut its full-year profit guidance on freight costs (Checkout, [Aug 4]).

EPS Upside Watch: Amrize — raised its revenue guidance on stronger demand from data centres (S&P Global, [Aug 7]). Barrick — earnings are expected to grow (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 3]), with gold up 7.2% over four weeks.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The oil shock is a margin gift for chemicals, not only a cost: the Iran war led to a profit surge for many chemical producers (Chemical & Engineering News, [Aug 7]), and Celanese beat on pricing and execution (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 5]). The sector's upside is broader than the miners.
Narrative: Rising long-end yields (10Y at 4.66%, +9 bps vs 4W) are a direct headwind and mortgage rates stay elevated; the sector cannot re-rate until the 10Y reverses.

Reported: Realty Income raised its 2026 growth targets (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). Public Storage raised its 2026 guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 3]). Zillow tumbled 13% after hours as its Q3 revenue guidance missed estimates (BigGo Finance, [Aug 6]).
EPS Upside Watch: Tritax Big Box — lifted its earnings target after powering up its data-centre pipeline with a £350m fund raise (QuotedData, [Aug 6]), the AI-infrastructure route to higher rents.
